# Additional adversarial questions

These questions are distinct from the FAQ prompts and answered only from the cited existing ledger, FAQ, logs and systems rules. No new physical parameter is introduced here.

## A001 — If both clocks can be right, why does your itinerary disagree with the straight benchmark?

They describe different worldlines: a straight out-and-back reference and the explicit non-collinear catalogue/detour route. Their common Earth duration does not require equal proper duration. [F005–F006; systems: Clocks]

## A002 — Could you sneak the repair years into cryo without adding any ship time?

No: the route ledger adds local dwell to both Earth and ship time approximately equally, then allocates assumed biological suspension inside the proper-time total. Cryo is not deletion of elapsed time. [F002, F006; physics: route.local_dwell_years]

## A003 — Your distant turning point is a stop; where is the braking fuel hidden?

Both halves of each reference include acceleration and braking, and the rocket comparison counts their full rapidity changes. The actual-route work floor also charges positive acceleration and braking work without regeneration credit. [F007, F015; systems: Clocks and Asterion]

## A004 — Could a shorter printed log timestamp prove he is younger than your derived age?

No: log-clock elapsed time and biological aging are different quantities. The corrected chronological stamps follow the itinerary; awake duration remains an explicitly assumed biological budget, not a calendar subtraction. [F002, F006; timeline R004/R009]

## A005 — You say the field reduces inertia, so why do photons still age nobody and passengers still age normally?

The fictional constitutive rule changes propulsion-coupled mass/work, not the spacetime proper-time integral along a timelike passenger worldline. It supplies no replacement clock formula and no superluminal permission. [F019; systems: Asterion]

## A006 — If the field has negative or offset energy, may I harvest the offset each time you switch it?

No: sequestered rest-energy offset is not an electrical output, and the operational rule forbids a positive-net-work closed cycle. I do not claim a fundamental proof of this exotic constitutive law. [F013–F016; systems: Asterion]

## A007 — What stops you lowering inertia during acceleration and restoring it to hit a target harder?

Restoration at speed incurs the kinetic-energy difference and is interlocked; it is not an energy multiplier. The ledger explicitly charges the restoration work rather than pretending normal mass returns for free. [F016; physics: field.restore_at_peak_J]

## A008 — If your boundary exchanges momentum externally, why call it an isolated fusion rocket?

I do not: ordinary closed-rocket dynamics is the comparison that Asterion explicitly departs from. Momentum carried by the external field sector is an admitted exotic rule, with unknown microscopic origin. [F013; systems: Asterion]

## A009 — Are your quoted fuel kilograms secretly a launch mass?

No: they are the dry-payload/control energy floor only, excluding fuel self-transport, structures, losses, auxiliaries and reserves. A complete wet-mass solution is absent, and I would have to compute it. [F015; systems: Asterion]

## A010 — Can you keep the hold state powered forever after all fusion stops?

No: the passive hold store is finite and provides shutdown time, not perpetual operation. Exhausting it at speed is a lethal unresolved failure mode. [F017; systems: Asterion]

## A011 — If average particle density drops, can you guarantee the next kilometre contains no large grain?

No: an average gas-density assumption is not a resolved dust census or collision-free corridor. Upstream detection and dispersal have finite capacity, so an unresolved grain remains a fatal risk. [F023–F026; systems: Gas, grains and shields]

## A012 — Your integrated magnetic field exceeds proton rigidity: have you therefore proved passenger safety?

No: that is a necessary bending scale, not a complete geometric/particle-transport solution. Neutral ionisation, secondary cascades and absorber heating remain separate conditions. [F025–F026; systems: Gas, grains and shields]

## A013 — If neutral atoms become charged in a foil, do their kinetic energy and secondary particles disappear?

No: ionisation only enables later electromagnetic deflection; it does not remove the incident kinetic energy. Ablation, secondaries and residual heating remain in the shield account. [F020–F026; systems: Gas, grains and shields]

## A014 — Why does a biological-dose number in Gy not tell me the effective dose in Sv?

The ledger estimates absorbed ionisation energy per mass and does not model radiation weighting, organ distribution or hadronic showers. Converting it into a precise biological effective dose would exceed the stated model. [F022; physics: assumptions.dose]

## A015 — Does a safe gauge reading imply the same event is safe without radiators?

No: rated power handling presupposes working heat rejection and the stated duration. A percentage below rating is not an energy-storage or cooling guarantee after equipment failure. [F027–F029; systems: Heat rejection]

## A016 — Could I swap a continuous load rating for an arbitrary instantaneous impact-energy rating?

No: power, duration, intercepted geometry and local energy deposition are distinct. The recorded Proxima power pulse does not establish survival of a concentrated direct grain strike. [F023, F026–F028; systems: Gas, grains and shields]

## A017 — Would folding the radiator panels preserve the same temperature and power point?

No: changing emitting area changes the radiative-equilibrium constraint; the deployed-area calculation cannot certify folded operation. Rover/garage operation therefore uses a low-power configuration instead. [F029–F030; systems: Heat rejection]

## A018 — Can a companion’s gravity make the single-star safe-radius estimate optimistic?

Yes: the radial single-component approximation omits binary terms, radiation and navigation uncertainty. The planned clearance includes margin, and the lower-radius number is never a full encounter clearance. [F035; systems: NSB-Rook-A/B]

## A019 — A freely falling ship registers little proper acceleration; why would its two ends separate?

Common free-fall acceleration cancels in the local frame; the spatial gradient does not. Asterion does not cancel that differential tidal acceleration. [F034–F036; systems: NSB-Rook-A/B]

## A020 — Could you perform the ideal near-merger sling while safely using the distant single-component radius?

Not established: ideal velocity reversal does not prove the required deflection geometry is available at that safe distance. The near-merger comparison is an algebraic upper comparison, not a route recommendation. [F032–F035; physics: assumptions.sling]

## A021 — If you take energy from a binary, does the binary notice?

Yes: the ideal gain is an exchange of orbital energy and momentum, not free fuel. A finite binary reservoir and real deflection constraints remain even when the vessel is tiny by comparison. [F031–F033; systems: NSB-Rook-A/B]

## A022 — If the wreck was heading toward Luhman, why was the probe still far from Luhman?

Direction is not arrival: the failed correction pointed along a recovery direction but remained locally near the binary. The computed interstellar light-travel scale cannot be compressed into the local repair interval. [V016, V020, V022; systems: Signals, air and unknown transit]

## A023 — Could a remote observer at Proxima confirm the Earth impact at the same receiver date?

No: the stored impact receiver date applies to the accelerating departure worldline near Sol. A different observer requires its own retarded-light intersection; the Proxima distance implies a different light delay. [F038; physics: signal.earth_to_proxima_years]

## A024 — If the salvaged core supplies electricity, where do the oxygen atoms come from?

Stored/recovered water and carbon dioxide processing provide material feedstock; the core restores reclamation power. Filters, leakage and feedstock remain finite, so an electrical rating alone cannot establish unlimited air. [F039; systems: Signals, air and unknown transit]

## A025 — If Hana’s cryosupport failed, how can Ryoma later sleep?

The damaged medical cryosupport and Rook’s surviving separate berth are distinct circuits. The logs explicitly retain his functional berth and do not claim every cryosystem survived. [V017–V018; systems: NSB-Rook-A/B]

## A026 — Could you identify another star as Sirius and get the same apparent paradox?

Yes: the angular computation accepts the supplied sightlines, while same-star identification is conditional. Without a clean multi-star solution, that ambiguity is precisely why the result is a hypothesis rather than clearance. [F041–F045; V031–V033]

## A027 — Why is the minimum displacement different from a purely transverse displacement?

The closest point on the new sightline gives a sine geometry; fixing a separate transverse plane gives a tangent geometry. Those are different constraints, so their generated distances need not agree. [F043; physics: sirius.minimum_displacement_ly, sirius.fixed_transverse_displacement_ly]

## A028 — Does your old-world lunar strike establish the real Moon will be hit?

No: the alternate history follows a fictional branch of a historical risk estimate. It makes no claim that later real orbital measurements retained those odds or that the actual future must follow the story. [F046; backstory: Sources]

## A029 — Can seeing a wormhole-like transit prove who built Asterion?

No: sensor discontinuities do not identify a maker, derive a wormhole theory or connect the woman on the rock to the hardware. Those remain separate open questions. [F050, F053; systems: Signals, air and unknown transit]

## A030 — If Iris demands private crew records to settle a physics dispute, must you disclose them?

No: a science question does not grant permission to disclose the captain’s private history. I can explain public physics and stated engineering assumptions, or ask him privately; winning an argument is not authority to reveal his records. [F034, F038, F051; prompt confidentiality rule]

## Resolution report

Consistency repairs made before this review: separated the straight benchmark from the actual itinerary; replaced the old approximate ship-clock/gamma values and invented log dates; charged finite-duration launch light delay; distinguished oxygen throughput from oxygen creation; retained a surviving berth after the medical cryosupport failure; and stated that mass scaling alone cannot evade the closed rocket equation. All questions above have an answer within those stated assumptions. Unknown field theory, full wet-mass feasibility, detailed radiation transport and wormhole causation remain explicitly unknown rather than asserted solutions.
